_about: Craft notes per tool: what it's for, what each input is in the picture, which settings matter and how they pull on each other, what people change when a result is wrong, and what it pairs with. src/knowledge.ts merges these with each workflow's own manifest and graph (models, nodes, every setting) into the cards the app shows (Create > How it works) and the AI editor and director read. Notes are starting points unless a doc says they were measured (docs/art-playbook.md rule 6). Keys of `settings` are param names or "<node>.<input>" node settings.

video.control.role: Films a shot that follows a control video exactly (layout, motion, camera), in the look of a styled first frame. The heart of directed video: the director's stage, blender.render or real footage drive it.

inputs.control: The motion and layout: a depth video (white near, black far), OpenPose skeletons, edges, or a mix (video.control-mix). Or plain footage with estimateDepth.
inputs.image: The first frame in the finished look. It sets the style, the characters and the light; the control sets where things are.

settings.prompt: Describe what happens and what it sounds like, not the picture (the image carries the look). Dialogue in quotes.
settings.strength: How strictly the video follows the control (0-1). Lower it (0.6-0.8) when stand-ins or rough depth make things stiff or blobby; keep 1 for exact camera moves.
settings.imageStrength: How strictly frame 1 matches the image. Lower it a little if the first frames freeze or the style fights the control.
settings.estimateDepth: On for plain footage: MoGe reads its depth first. Off for depth or pose videos you made.
settings.129:195.strength_model: The IC-LoRA's strength (how much the control conditioning counts at all). With strength, the second knob for 'follows the control too literally'.
settings.steps: 8 is the distilled default. More steps rarely help this model; change the sampler or scheduler before steps.
settings.129:704.sampler_name: euler_ancestral by default. euler gives calmer, less noisy motion.
settings.129:115.frame_idx: Which frame the control guide starts on (0).

iterate: Characters melt into the background: raise imageStrength, describe them more clearly in the first frame, or add pose to the control (video.control-mix).
Stiff or puppet-like motion: lower strength to 0.7-0.85 so the model can add life.
Wrong length: the control video sets it (8n + 1 frames at 24 fps); seconds only trims.
Sound missing or off: describe the sounds in the prompt; LTX makes audio with the video.

video.control-wan.role: The same idea as video.control on Wan 2.2 Fun Control: 16 fps, no sound, slower (about 7 minutes a shot), sometimes steadier faces.
iterate: Use it when LTX keeps changing a face; interpolate x2 afterwards for 32 fps.

image.control.role: Paints a finished picture over the structure of another (Z-Image Turbo + Fun Union ControlNet: canny, HED, depth, pose, MLSD). Turns a grey-box render, the director's stage frame, a sketch or a depth map into the look, keeping the layout.

inputs.image: The control: a render, sketch, depth or pose map. Its shapes and placement are kept.

settings.prompt: The whole look: place, era, style, light, and each character's appearance. Say 'keep the layout'.

iterate: Characters don't match the cast: describe each one by position ('on the left, a knight in silver armor').
Too close to the grey render: describe materials and light more; the control keeps only structure.

image.edit.role: Changes a picture with words while keeping its design (Qwen-Image-Edit 2511). Also: other angles, A-pose, recolors, and painting a render in a look with reference sheets (the film pipeline's keyframe).

inputs.images: Up to three: the picture to change first, then references (character sheets) it should match.

settings.prompt: What to change, and what to keep ('keep the composition and poses exactly').
settings.width: With height: the output size. Non-square inputs are padded on grey, never stretched.
settings.denoise: How much it may change (lower keeps more).

iterate: Drifts off-model: add the character sheet as image 2 and say 'match image 2'.
Changes too much: lower denoise or say exactly what must stay.

image.generate.role: A new picture from words (Z-Image Turbo): concept art, props, textures (seamless), first frames.

settings.prompt: Subject, setting, style, light, camera. Specific beats long.

iterate: Characters for 3D: full body, front view, A-pose, plain light background.

video.i2v.role: Brings a picture to life (Wan 2.2): the picture is frame 1, the prompt is the motion.

inputs.end: Optional last frame: the clip travels from start to end.

settings.prompt: A description of motion, not an instruction: who moves, how, where to, and the camera. 'Make it fly' on a bird gave a still bird; 'the bird spreads its wings and takes off, big clear continuous motion' flew (A/B, 2026-10-29).

iterate: Nothing moves: describe the motion bigger and earlier ('right away').
Camera drifts: say 'locked-off camera' or the move you want.

video.t2v.role: A clip from words alone. Least control: use the director (video.control) when placement or camera matter.

settings.prompt: Shot type, subject, action, camera move, light, sound.

video.extend.role: Carries a shot on from a frame (MiniMax H3). Grab the last frame with video.frame ('last') first.

video.keyframes.role: A scene that passes through two or three keyframes you give, with a reference for the character. The bridge between storyboard stills and motion.

video.motion.role: A still character performs the motion of a driving clip (Wan Animate 2).

video.animate.role: Character motion transfer: a reference picture moves like a driving video.

video.replace.role: Your character takes over a real performance (SCAIL-2): keeps the actor's motion, face and timing.

video.talk.role: A portrait talks along to a voice line (InfiniteTalk). Close-ups and dialogue.

inputs.image: The face, framed as the shot.

video.lipsync.role: A character says a line with head and body motion (LTX-2.3).

video.perform.role: A character performs a line in their own voice (LTX-2.3 ID-LoRA).

video.control-mix.role: Mixes depth, pose and edges control videos into one (the brightest wins, pose and edges dimmed). The layout from depth plus the lines from pose and edges.

settings.weights: One per video: [1, 0.8, 0.5] for depth, pose, edges.

video.upscale.role: A sharper 4x clip. Slow on long clips: upscale the keeper, not every take.

video.interpolate.role: In-between frames for smoother motion (x2 makes 16 fps Wan into 32).

video.frame.role: One frame as a picture: 'first', 'last' or seconds. The bridge from a clip back to image tools.

image.viewsheet.role: Back, left and right views of a front cutout, checked by Claude to be the same character, laid as a 4-view sheet. Always before 3D (one view makes the model guess the back).

inputs.image: The FRONT view, cut out (image.remove-background's cutout, never its mask).

settings.form: What it is; 'robot' keeps every limb apart in each view.

mesh.views3d.role: A textured 3D model (GLB, PBR) from a 4-view sheet (Pixal3D multi-view + TRELLIS.2). The way Gen turns pictures into 3D.
iterate: Smeared back: the views didn't match; remake the sheet.
Dense mesh: blender.character retopo, then mesh.rig.

mesh.textured.role: A textured model from ONE picture: props and blockouts only (allowSingleView). Characters use the 4-view path.

mesh.rig.role: A skeleton and skinning for a GLB so it can move (humanoid: Mixamo bones; creatures: SkinTokens). Needs the SSH GPU fleet.

motion.from-text.role: A humanoid animation from words, on your rigged character (Kimodo SOMA, HY-Motion). Needs the SSH GPU fleet.

settings.prompt: One clear action with its manner ('walks cautiously, looks over both shoulders, crouches').

image.panorama.role: A seamless 360° equirect environment: a skybox, or the director's set backdrop.

texture.maps.role: Material maps from a seamless texture: albedo, normal, roughness and more. Make it seamless first (image.generate seamless, or image.tile).

image.remove-background.role: Cuts the subject out on the GPU. Returns [mask, cutout]: chains must take '$stepN:cutout'.

image.cutout.role: Cuts the subject out (rembg/BiRefNet on CPU).

image.relight.role: New lighting on a picture, keeping it otherwise. Matches a keyframe to the scene's light.

image.restore.role: SeedVR2 restore and 4x upscale. Heavy: a 1280x704 frame becomes 5120x2816.

image.segment.role: Masks of what you name (SAM 3): 'the car', 'every person'. Feeds repaint, change and composite.

audio.music.role: Music from a description (ACE-Step 1.5), with lyrics or instrumental.

audio.voice.role: A spoken line (ElevenLabs premade voices in the app). Feeds video.talk, lipsync and the timeline.

audio.sfx.role: A sound effect from words, with a length; loop for ambiences.

quality.identity.role: Is this the same person? ArcFace face distance (insightface buffalo_l, CPU) from the best-matching face in each checked frame to a character's references. The identity check of the making loop and Gen Bench.

inputs.file: The picture or clip to check. Several faces in it are fine: the one that matches best is taken as the character.
inputs.refs: The character's sheet, front and portrait. A cutout or a full sheet both work; every face of about the same size on a sheet counts.

settings.frames: Frames sampled from a clip (8). More frames find a face that drifts for a moment; the spread says how steady it is.

iterate: Measured on this PC, 2026-10-31 (docs/bench.md): an altered copy of the same face 0.06, the right face picked out of a group photo 0.02, a different person 1.04 (insightface's own sample photos). Target (Face Consistency Benchmark): real video about 0.08, pass under 0.15.
distance null: no face found (too small, turned away, or a stylised face the detector misses). Check faces and refFaces in the result before trusting a pass.
Over 0.15 on a picture: give the sheet as a reference to image.edit / image.control and paste the fixed description unchanged.
A low mean but a high spread (over 0.05): the face drifts mid-clip; shorten the shot or lower the motion.

quality.checklist.role: Does the output follow the brief? The brief becomes 4-8 concrete yes/no questions, a vision model answers each from the output (4 frames of a clip), and the score is the share answered yes (0.85 to pass).

inputs.refs: Who or what should appear, so 'is it Maya' can be answered.

settings.brief: Write what must be visible: who, what they hold, the setting, the time of day, the framing, any text.
settings.questions: Your own questions when the brief's automatic ones miss what matters.

iterate: A question answered no: say that thing plainly and first in the prompt next try (quality.assess's fix does this).
Questions that can't be seen (a sound, a smell, a thought) always come back no: keep briefs visual.

quality.assess.role: Every check for one output: identity against the cast's references, the brief's questions, the obvious faults for its kind (hands, faces, text, blank frames and flicker, a model's geometry and triangle budget, a sound's silence and clipping) and the look. Pass or fail, and a fix for the next try. Run it on every take before a person sees it.

inputs.identityRefs: The character's references (none: identity isn't checked).

settings.brief: What it should be, in words.
settings.style: The look in words, with or instead of the style board.
settings.thresholds: { identity: 0.15, checklist: 0.85, style: 0.7 }. Raise them for a hero shot, never lower them to make a take pass.

iterate: Feed `fix` into the next try's prompt or settings: it names what failed and what usually fixes it.
errors lists checks that couldn't run (no face models, the AI unavailable): they don't fail the take, they measured nothing.
